title: A flow-cytometry-based assessment of global protein synthesis in human senescent cells
protocol: Thaw and seed IMR90 cells in a 10 cm culture plate with 10 mL complete culture medium.
Incubate the cells in a physiological O2 incubator for 1–3 days until they reach approximately 90% confluence.
Discard the culture medium and briefly rinse the cells with 5–10 mL prewarmed 1× DPBS to remove all traces of serum that contains trypsin inhibitors.
Add 1 mL prewarmed trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) to the cells and hold at 37°C until cell layer is dispersed.
Neutralize trypsin-EDTA by adding 9 mL prewarmed complete culture medium and gently pipette 10 to 15 times to resuspend the cells.
Check cell number using a cell counter.
Seed the cells into 6-well culture plates at a density of 1.2 X 10^5 cells/well.
Add complete culture medium to a final volume of 2 mL/well.
Incubate the cells in a physiological O2 incubator for 16 h.
Check cell confluence to be approximately 10% before applying DNA damage.
Induce senescence in IMR90 cells by irradiation when the culture is appropriately confluent.
Monitor cellular hypertrophy and other morphological changes indicative of senescence.
Expose the cells to a single ionizing radiation dose of 12 Gy using an appropriate irradiator system that provides controlled dosing.
Maintain normal (non-senescence-induced) cells as a control.
Replace the culture medium with 2 mL fresh, pre-warmed complete culture medium 24 hours after irradiation.
Replace exhausted culture medium with 2 mL of fresh, prewarmed complete culture medium every 3-4 days.

Monitor the expression of senescence markers such as Senescence-Associated Beta-Galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) activity, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors (e.g., p21 and p16), and Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP).
Sub-culture cells at a ratio of 1:2 if they become confluent (>80%) within 2-4 days after irradiation to allow robust senescent phenotypes, including hypertrophy.
Avoid sub-culturing when cells start to show signs of senescence hypertrophy (generally around 4-5 days post-irradiation) due to sensitivity to trypsinization.
Replace complete culture medium with 1 mL prewarmed methionine-free medium.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Prepare a fresh L-AHA working solution by diluting the stock solution in prewarmed methionine-free medium (100 μM final concentration).
Label cells with 1 mL of 100 μM L-AHA for 30 min at 37°C.
Discard the L-AHA culture medium and briefly rinse cells with 1–2 mL prewarmed 1× DPBS per well to remove all traces of serum.
Add 250 µL prewarmed trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) to cells and hold at 37°C for 2–3 min until cell layer is dispersed.
Add 750 μL prewarmed methionine-free medium to cells and gently pipette 10 to 15 times to resuspend cells.
Collect cell suspension in U-bottom FACS tubes.
Centrifuge at 300 × g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatants.
Wash cells with cold 1× DPBS.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of cold 1× DPBS per tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Gently discard supernatants by pipetting.
Fix cells with paraformaldehyde.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde (w/v in DPBS) per tube.
Incubate cells for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Centrifuge at 800 × g, 4°C for 10 minutes.
Gently discard supernatants by pipetting.
Permeabilize cells with permeabilization buffer by resuspending in 200 μL of 0.5% Triton X-100 per tube.
Incubate cells for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Centrifuge cells at 800 × g, 4°C for 10 min.
Gently discard supernatants by pipetting without aspiration.
Prepare the L-AHA click reaction cocktail as described in materials and equipment.
Add 200 μL of L-AHA click reaction solution per tube.
Resuspend cell pellet and incubate for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash cells twice with 1% BSA in 1× DPBS: resuspend cells in 500 μL of 1% BSA in 1× DPBS per tube.
Centrifuge cells at 800 × g, 4°C for 10 min.
Gently discard supernatants by pipetting.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL 1% FBS in 1× DBPS.
Place all tubes on ice in the dark.
Turn on the Attune NxT Acoustic Focusing Cytometer.
Draw the gate by the forward (FSC-A) and side scatter profiling (SSC-A) that defines the main live cell population, excluding cellular debris and dead cells with the Attune Nxt Software.
For the live cell population gated in step 25, record L-AHA incorporation (AFdye405) for at least 10,000 events.
Quantify L-AHA incorporation by measuring the median value of fluorescence with FlowJo software.
Open FlowJo software and drag the data such as fcs format into a workspace.
Double-click the icon of any data in the list and draw the gate that includes live cells but excludes cell debris and dead cells.
Name this population as “live”.
Apply this gating to all samples by dragging the “live” icon in the list to the icon of “all samples”.
Double click the "live" icon in any sample.
Change the horizontal axis into the channel recording L-AHA incorporation (AFdye405).
Apply this change to all samples by dragging the modified icon to the "all samples" icon.
Click the icon of “Layout Editor” and drag the “live” icon to create graphical reports.
Double click the graph with the Layout Editor to customize the look of the graphical reports.
Right-click the “live” icon and click “Add statistics”.
Select “Median” for the channel recording L-AHA incorporation (AFdye405).
Click “Add” to add the median statistics.
Apply the median statistics to all samples by dragging the “Median” icon in the list to the “live” icon under all samples.
Export the file in excel format.
